disease_label_per_paper: Concurrent acute pancreatitis and calculous cholecystitis
presentation_summary: 83-year-old woman with ischemic heart disease, asthma, hypertension, and ex-tobacco smoking presented with sudden severe epigastric burning pain radiating to the back.
Pain was associated with nausea and vomiting; vital signs were reported as normal.
Exam showed severe epigastric tenderness and moderate right upper quadrant tenderness.
Serology showed WBC 12.6 x 10^9/L, CRP 170, lipase 13000 U/L, bilirubin 12 umol/L, ALT 92 U/L, AST 146 U/L, ALP 89 U/L, and GGT 117 U/L.
Ultrasound showed gallstones and gallbladder wall thickening; CT showed pancreatitis with moderate peripancreatic fat stranding and no necrosis, abscess, or pseudocyst.
